quote.text: Gold is money. Everything else is credit.
quote.author: J. Pierpont Morgan, distilled from his testimony to the U.S. House "Pujo" Committee on the money trust, December 1912

stories.headline: The Highest Inflation in Nearly Two Years — and the Number That Undershot It
stories.dek: July's headline rate hit 2.2 per cent and core reached 2.0, the fastest since October 2024. Read past the headline: both prints came in below what economists expected, momentum fell month-on-month, and the jump was a switch flicked at the electricity meter, not a hot economy.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Big Picture
stories.headline: Gold Clears a Record, the Long Bond Gets Rescued Again, and Friday Belongs to a New Chair
stories.dek: Bullion took out a fresh high as the thirty-year yield — a nineteen-year peak days earlier — eased only because the Treasury signalled it would fund more of its own buying. The dollar is soft into Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole, where the market prices a hold and, at the tail, a hike — not a cut.

stories.kicker: The Rabbit Hole · The Invitation — Film Photography
stories.headline: Thirty-Six Frames, No Screen, and a Wait — the Constraint Is the Whole Product
stories.dek: You load a light-proof roll, get a fixed number of shots, and cannot see a single one until chemistry and a scanner give them back. In a world of infinite free frames, film sells the one thing digital can't: scarcity, deliberation, and a decades-old machine you buy once.

stories.headline: For the First Time Since the War, Syria and Israel Sit Down to Turn the Strikes Off
stories.dek: On Sunday a Syrian delegation led by the foreign minister — and, tellingly, both intelligence chiefs — met Israel's Mossad director in Jordan under American mediation. On the table: a "special operations room" to stop the shooting, and the security deal the two sides had almost signed before the wider war blew it up.

stories.kicker: The Atelier · Buy It Once — No. 9 · Bed Linen
stories.headline: Buy the Cloth, Not the Count — and Definitely Not the Logo
stories.dek: You spend a third of your life against these sheets, and almost everything the label shouts about is a lie. The quality is decided by a fibre you can't see and a weave you can feel — and in a Singapore bedroom, the thousand-dollar sateen is the wrong answer.

stories.headline: A Chinese Lab Built a Model Too Good at Finding Holes — So It Kept the Keys
stories.dek: Z.ai shipped GLM-5.3 this month, then held the open weights for two weeks to harden them, after the model scored top of its class at discovering software vulnerabilities and reportedly turned up a serious one in a popular coding tool. An open-weights lab voluntarily withholding weights is the sovereignty story of the week.

stories.headline: A Three-Hundred-Dollar Cinema on Your Face — the Morning a Thousand-Dollar Watch Is One Livestream Away
stories.dek: VITURE's Pro 2 glasses ship with real reviews and a price cut that undercuts the entry field; Garmin's "Play Harder" event, today, is expected to drop the Fēnix 9 and Enduro 4. One you can buy; the other you can only watch.

stories.headline: A Solar Formula One Watch for a Farewell Lap — and What You're Really Paying For
stories.dek: TAG Heuer marked Zandvoort's last Dutch Grand Prix with two limited Formula 1 Solargraphs: 38 millimetres, light-charged, a genuinely useful movement in a genuinely disposable price bracket. The horology is entry-level; the premium is the story.

stories.headline: Venice Opens on a Young Press Baron; a Tennis Elegy Lands Before the Open
stories.dek: The Lido raises its curtain on Danny Boyle's Murdoch origin story and a competition thick with debuts; on streaming, a Djokovic documentary times itself to the US Open — and keeps the warts discreetly off-camera.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · Raising Them Well
stories.headline: The Study That Ends at Exactly Twelve — and the Finding That Reframes the Panic
stories.dek: A new paper of more than ten thousand children measures phone ownership against depression, sleep and weight at precisely the age of a Secondary One student. The more useful result, from a separate study, is that it isn't the hour-count that tracks the harm — it's the addictive pattern.

stories.headline: The Strength Dose With a Ceiling: Ninety Minutes Buys the Longevity, and More Buys Nothing
stories.dek: A thirty-year study of nearly a hundred and fifty thousand people found the sweet spot for lifting sits at ninety to a hundred and twenty minutes a week — and, unusually, that the benefit flatlines above it. Two fifty-minute sessions is the high-return dose; the medal for overtraining doesn't exist.

stories.headline: A Sprint-Weekend Grand Prix, a Stadium Autumn, and a Kyushu Sumo Run Worth the Flight
stories.dek: The dated agenda through year-end — Singapore's first-ever Formula One Sprint, a dense run of arena nights, and the Tokyo and regional fixtures a Japan-loving family should book now, with the twelve-year-old's picks flagged.

stories.headline: The People's Central Bank
stories.dek: Across Vietnam, young office workers are turning payday into gold day — buying bullion by the tenth-of-a-tael on their phones and queuing in the rain for mini-bars. It reads like a savings-app story. Look again: a generation is quietly building its own gold-backed pension, exactly as the state races to take that gold back.
